sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This time of year, right in the middle of the holiday season,
sentences.zh: 每到一年中的这个时候，正值假日季的中段，

sentences.en: there's a beloved frenzied tradition playing out in Filipino households all around the world.
sentences.zh: 全世界的菲律宾家庭都会上演一个备受喜爱而又疯狂的传统。

sentences.en: Here to explain is reporter Gabrielle Burbay.
sentences.zh: 接下来由记者加布里埃尔·伯贝为您解释。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Lola.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗拉。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: That, by the way, is Gabby's grandma.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，那是加比的奶奶。

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I just came from the church.
sentences.zh: 我刚从教堂回来。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, I called my Lola to ask if she would be taking part in this annual tradition.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我打电话给罗拉，问她是否会参加这项年度传统。

sentences.en: Okay, so are you sending a Balik Bayan box this year?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么你今年要寄回国大礼箱吗？

sentences.en: Do you know what Balik Bayan box is?
sentences.zh: 你知道什么是回国大礼箱吗？

sentences.en: Are you quizzing me?
sentences.zh: 你在考我吗？

sentences.en: The Balik Bayan box is the box that Filipinos abroad send to their relatives back in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 回国大礼箱就是海外菲律宾人寄给远在菲律宾的亲戚的箱子。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's Balik is returning and Bayan is home, like Philippines.
sentences.zh: “巴里克”是回家，“拜彦”是家园，就像菲律宾那样。

sentences.en: That's my home.
sentences.zh: 那是我的家。

sentences.en: A Balik Bayan box is a huge cardboard box, usually over 100 pounds,
sentences.zh: 回国大礼箱是一个巨大的纸板箱，通常重达100磅以上，

sentences.en: that Filipinos living all over the world send to family members who are still living in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的菲律宾人将它寄给仍然住在菲律宾的家庭成员。

sentences.en: The word Balik Bayan literally means homecoming in Tagalog.
sentences.zh: 在他加禄语中，“巴里克·拜彦”字面意思是荣归故里。

sentences.en: When I was in the Philippines, it was Uncle Dennis who came here in America firSt.
sentences.zh: 我在菲律宾时，是丹尼斯叔叔先来美国的。

sentences.en: He was the one who first sent us a Balik Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个给我们寄回国大礼箱的人。

sentences.en: To me, the Balik Bayan box, we're always looking forward to it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，回国大礼箱，我们总是翘首以盼。

sentences.en: Today, my Lola lives in the U.S., which means she's usually the one sending Balik Bayan boxes.
sentences.zh: 如今，我的罗拉住在美国，这意味着通常是她来寄回国大礼箱。

sentences.en: But when she was still living in the Philippines, she remembers receiving them.
sentences.zh: 但当她还住在菲律宾时，她还记得收到箱子的情景。

sentences.en: Do you remember the delivery person walking up to the door?
sentences.zh: 你还记得送货员走向门口的时候吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we were so excited.
sentences.zh: 对，我们太兴奋了。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: The Balik Bayan box is usually delivered right to your door.
sentences.zh: 回国大礼箱通常直接送到你家门口。

sentences.en: Someone knocked on my door, and the door I said, and it's a delivery.
sentences.zh: 有人敲我的门，我应了一声，是快递到了。

sentences.en: June, Ariel, the box from Burden is here.
sentences.zh: 琼，阿里尔，伯登的箱子到了。

sentences.en: The family gathers around the box.
sentences.zh: 全家人围聚在箱子周围。

sentences.en: So they all went down, opened the box, and they were so happy, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都下楼来，打开箱子，他们真是太高兴了。

sentences.en: And the box is filled with lots and lots of stuff from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 箱子里装满了从美国带回来的各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: They are full of chocolates, usually goods coming from Costco, the hand-me-down clothes, like jackets.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了巧克力，通常是好市多买的商品，还有像夹克这样的二手衣服。

sentences.en: Sneakers, socks, books, electronics, Game Boy, even toothpaste, shampoo.
sentences.zh: 运动鞋、袜子、书籍、电子产品、游戏机，甚至牙膏、洗发水。

sentences.en: And the most prized object in the box.
sentences.zh: 还有箱子里最珍贵的物品。

sentences.en: Oh, this, like the spam.
sentences.zh: 哦，这个，就像午餐肉。

sentences.en: Spam is very expensive in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 午餐肉在菲律宾非常贵。

sentences.en: Spam.
sentences.zh: 午餐肉。

sentences.en: And it's not just Gabby's family that does this.
sentences.zh: 不只是加比的家里人这么做。

sentences.en: 400,000 of these Balik Bayan boxes arrive in the Philippines from around the world every month.
sentences.zh: 每个月有40万个这样的回国大礼箱从世界各地运抵菲律宾。

sentences.en: But right now, with the holidays, it's the busiest season.
sentences.zh: 但现在正值假期，是最繁忙的季节。

sentences.en: Mothers sending to sons, brothers, sisters, hundreds of thousands of people waiting in the Philippines for their box.
sentences.zh: 母亲寄给儿子、兄弟、姐妹，成千上万的人在菲律宾等待着他们的箱子。

sentences.en: Hey guys, welcome back to my channel.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好，欢迎回到我的频道。

sentences.en: So for today's video, guys, I'm going to be showing you how I pack my Balik Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 那么在今天的视频里，我要向大家展示我是如何打包回国大礼箱的。

sentences.en: On YouTube, there are thousands of videos of people showing how to pack their box.
sentences.zh: 在YouTube上，有成千上万关于人们展示如何打包箱子的视频。

sentences.en: And the joys of Balik Bayan boxing and Balik Bayan unboxing.
sentences.zh: 还有打包和拆箱回国大礼箱的乐趣。

sentences.en: I don't know how did I fit everything inside this box.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是怎么把所有东西都塞进这个箱子里的。

sentences.en: So much work.
sentences.zh: 有太多的工作了。

sentences.en: But I'm very sure it's going to be worth it when I get there.
sentences.zh: 但我深信，当我到达那里时，这一切都是值得的。

sentences.en: Yay!
sentences.zh: 太棒了！

sentences.en: I've been waiting for so long, guys.
sentences.zh: 我等了太久了，伙计们。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Mommy?
sentences.zh: 妈妈？

sentences.en: You're sending what?
sentences.zh: 你要寄什么？

sentences.en: Oh my god.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪。

sentences.en: You called and told me, Anako, we sent you Balik Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 你打电话告诉我，孩子，我们给你寄了回国大礼箱。

sentences.en: I'm getting Balik Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 我收到了回国大礼箱。

sentences.en: Sent to me from my mama, bro.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈寄给我的，兄弟。

sentences.en: Clearly, Filipinos love the Balik Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 显然，菲律宾人非常热爱回国大礼箱。

sentences.en: But I didn't even realize that it was something that was unique to us until I traveled to the Philippines for the first time when I was 12.
sentences.zh: 但我甚至没有意识到这是我们独有的东西，直到我12岁第一次去菲律宾旅行。

sentences.en: I remember going to the airport in San Francisco, completely jittery, for my first long haul international flight.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时在旧金山机场，因为第一次进行长途国际航班而紧张不安。

sentences.en: And seeing this long line, only in front of Philippine Airlines,
sentences.zh: 我看到这条长长的队伍，只排在菲律宾航空公司柜台前，

sentences.en: where people were waiting for those high-powered saran wrap machines to get their cardboard boxes wrapped in layers and layers of plastic.
sentences.zh: 人们在那里排队等待使用那些强力的保鲜膜机，把他们的纸板箱缠上一层又一层的塑料膜。

sentences.en: And I remember looking around and thinking, huh, I wonder why do so many Filipino travelers have these massive cardboard boxes?
sentences.zh: 我记得环顾四周，心想，咦，为什么这么多菲律宾旅客都有这么大的纸板箱？

sentences.en: The reason Filipino travelers line up in the airport to wrap 100-pound-plus Balik Bayan boxes is the same reason why Filipino sons and daughters, mothers and aunts,
sentences.zh: 菲律宾旅客排队在机场打包重达100多磅的回国大礼箱的原因，和菲律宾的儿子女儿、母亲姑姑们，

sentences.en: often live oceans apart from one another.
sentences.zh: 常常天各一方生活在海洋两端的原因是一样的。

sentences.en: More than 10 million Filipinos live abroad, and over a million more leave the country every year.
sentences.zh: 超过1000万菲律宾人居住在海外，每年还有100多万人离开这个国家。

sentences.en: This migration of Filipinos abroad is also what gives the beloved, complicated Balik Bayan box, the homecoming box, its name.
sentences.zh: 菲律宾人的这种海外移民也是那个备受喜爱而又复杂的“回国大礼箱”（即返乡箱）名称的由来。

sentences.en: My father left in 1982, and he went specifically to Libya at that point to work in the construction industry.
sentences.zh: 我父亲在1982年离开，当时他特地去了利比亚从事建筑行业。

sentences.en: Anna Guevara is an expert in Filipino migration.
sentences.zh: 安娜·格瓦拉是菲律宾移民问题专家。

sentences.en: She's also from the Philippines, and like many Filipinos, grew up with a father working overseas.
sentences.zh: 她也来自菲律宾，和许多菲律宾人一样，成长于一个父亲在海外工作的家庭。

sentences.en: When Anna was around nine years old, her dad left the Philippines to work in the Middle East as a construction worker.
sentences.zh: 安娜大约九岁时，她父亲离开菲律宾前往中东当建筑工人。

sentences.en: She showed me a picture he sent her when he was in Libya.
sentences.zh: 她给我看了一张他还在利比亚时寄给她的照片。

sentences.en: It is a picture of the desert, you know, very bare piece of land, kind of reddish in color.
sentences.zh: 那是一张沙漠的照片，你知道的，是一片非常荒凉的土地，呈微红色。

sentences.en: And there's just one station that you can see, and that's where the workers were based.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到只有一个站点，那就是工人们的驻地。

sentences.en: He would write messages to Anna and her mom on the back of the photographs, telling them what he was doing, all the places he was seeing.
sentences.zh: 他会在照片背面给安娜和她妈妈写信，告诉她们他在做什么，以及他所看到的每一个地方。

sentences.en: It says,
sentences.zh: 上面写着，

sentences.en: Dear Mommy, husbands and wives call themselves Mommy and Daddy.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的妈妈，夫妻们互相称呼为妈妈和爸爸。

sentences.en: These are some of the terraces made by our men here.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们这里的男人们建造的一些梯田。

sentences.en: I intend to plant a huge billboard proclaiming
sentences.zh: 我打算竖起一块巨大的广告牌，宣告

sentences.en: handiwork of Filipino crusaders for Libyan progress and development with love.
sentences.zh: 带着爱意，这是菲律宾为利比亚繁荣发展而奋斗的先锋们的杰作。

sentences.en: What does he mean by Filipino crusaders?
sentences.zh: 他说的“菲律宾先锋”是什么意思？

sentences.en: I think they saw themselves as individuals who, you know, were building up a nation.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们把自己视为建设国家的一份子。

sentences.en: Not as crusaders building up Libya, but building up the Philippines as heroes willing to pack up, leave their family behind, and find work abroad to send money home.
sentences.zh: 不是作为建设利比亚的先锋，而是作为愿意收拾行囊、抛下家人、去海外寻找工作并将钱寄回家的英雄，来建设菲律宾。

sentences.en: I think they were quite aware that their remittances were of value to the country, that they were helping the country rise up from a really dire situation at the time.
sentences.zh: 我想他们非常清楚，他们的汇款对国家很有价值，他们正在帮助国家从当时真正可怕的困境中崛起。

sentences.en: Decades before the birth of the Balak Bayan box, remittances, where people abroad send money home,
sentences.zh: 在回国大礼箱诞生几十年前，海外务工人员将钱寄回家的汇款，

sentences.en: were a lifeline to families in the Philippines who were living through one of the worst economic crises the country had ever experienced.
sentences.zh: 一直是菲律宾家庭的生命线，当时他们正经历着该国历史上最严重的经济危机之一。

sentences.en: That story starts in 1898.
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于1898年。

sentences.en: The Philippines was a colony of Spain.
sentences.zh: 当时菲律宾是西班牙的殖民地。

sentences.en: Spain ruled the Philippines for nearly 400 years.
sentences.zh: 西班牙统治菲律宾近400年。

sentences.en: Then, in the late 19th century, the Filipino people rose up to fight for independence.
sentences.zh: 然后，在19世纪末，菲律宾人民奋起抗争以争取独立。

sentences.en: But they did not fight alone.
sentences.zh: 但他们并非孤军奋战。

sentences.en: The United States helped the Filipino people battle the Spanish colonizers.
sentences.zh: 美国帮助菲律宾人民抗击西班牙殖民者。

sentences.en: This was at a moment when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时正值美国

sentences.en: was in the midst of imperial expansion into former Spanish territories, like Puerto Rico and Guam.
sentences.zh: 向波多黎各和关岛等原西班牙领土进行帝国扩张的时期。

sentences.en: In the end, the Spanish loSt.
sentences.zh: 最终，西班牙战败了。

sentences.en: But rather than granting Filipinos their independence, the Spanish sold the Philippines to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但西班牙并没有给予菲律宾人独立，而是将菲律宾卖给了美国。

sentences.en: You hear then-President McKinley proclaim that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你听到时任总统麦金利宣称美国

sentences.en: is coming to the Philippines as friends, not enemies, and it is under this guise of benevolent assimilation.
sentences.zh: 是以朋友而非敌人的身份来到菲律宾，而这就是在仁慈同化的幌子下进行的。

sentences.en: At the time, the United States claimed that benevolent assimilation was somehow magically different from Spain's colonialism.
sentences.zh: 当时，美国声称这种仁慈的同化在某种程度上神奇地不同于西班牙的殖民主义。

sentences.en: You know, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你看，美国

sentences.en: saw the Philippines as just this collection of tribes.
sentences.zh: 将菲律宾仅仅看作是这样一个由各个部落组成的集合体。

sentences.en: And that through this benevolent assimilation, America can transform this citizenry into a more disciplined, a more rule-bound population who would be, you know,
sentences.zh: 并认为通过这种仁慈的同化，美国可以将这些公民转变为一个更有纪律、更守规矩的群体，他们会是，你知道的，

sentences.en: fitting of the U.S., of its empire.
sentences.zh: 配得上美国及其帝国的。

sentences.en: In an effort to basically erase Filipino culture and replace it with American ideals, the United States set up American hospitals, American schools with American teachers.
sentences.zh: 为了从根本上抹杀菲律宾文化并用美国的理念取而代之，美国建立了美国医院、配备美国教师的美国学校。

sentences.en: You know, it even went as far as teaching Filipinos how to eat, you know, proper etiquette when you're at a dinner table, how to speak, how to pronounce certain words.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它甚至发展到教菲律宾人如何吃饭，比如在餐桌上的正确礼仪，如何说话，如何发某些词的音。

sentences.en: So it looked like a systematic erasure of the Philippines, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上看起来是对菲律宾的系统性抹杀。

sentences.en: But President McKinley's project of benevolent assimilation had a bigger objective beyond just westernizing Filipinos.
sentences.zh: 但麦金利总统的仁慈同化计划有着更宏大的目标，不仅仅是让菲律宾人西方化。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: needed farm workers.
sentences.zh: 需要农场工人。

sentences.en: It was very strategic to turn to your colonized subjects as, you know, labor supply.
sentences.zh: 把被殖民的子民当作劳动力来源是非常具有战略眼光的。

sentences.en: The United States quickly saw that the Philippines' most lucrative resource was Filipinos.
sentences.zh: 美国很快发现菲律宾最有利可图的资源就是菲律宾人。

sentences.en: At the turn of the 20th century, Filipinos, mainly men, migrated en masse to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪之交，菲律宾人（主要是男性）作为农场工人大量移民到美国

sentences.en: mainland and Hawaii as farm workers.
sentences.zh: 本土和夏威夷。

sentences.en: The first bricks were laid for what would become a major immigration pathway for Filipinos seeking work overseas.
sentences.zh: 为后来寻求海外工作的菲律宾人开辟一条主要移民途径奠定了基础。

sentences.en: In 1935, the U.S.
promised the Philippines independence at the end of a 10-year period.
sentences.zh: 承诺在10年期满后给予菲律宾独立。

sentences.en: But before those 10 years were up, the Philippines was then occupied again by the Japanese during World War II.
sentences.zh: 但在这10年期满之前，菲律宾在二战期间再次被日本占领。

sentences.en: After the war, the country struggled to gain funding in a global economy.
sentences.zh: 战后，该国在全球经济中艰难地获得资金。

sentences.en: By the 1960s, nearly half of the country lived in poverty.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪60年代，近一半的人口生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: Ferdinand Marcos Sr.
sentences.zh: 费迪南德·马科斯

sentences.en: was elected president.
sentences.zh: 当选总统。

sentences.en: The election of Marcos ushered in one of the darkest periods of Philippine history.
sentences.zh: 马科斯的当选开启了菲律宾历史上最黑暗的时期之一。

sentences.en: One that would not only lead to the creation of the Balak Bayan Baks, but would also reshape the Philippines forever.
sentences.zh: 这段历史不仅导致了回国大礼箱的诞生，也将永远重塑菲律宾。

sentences.en: At that time, the Philippines was an economic leader in the region.
sentences.zh: 当时，菲律宾是该地区的经济领头羊。

sentences.en: And Marcos ran on a campaign promise to bring even more jobs, development, and economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 马科斯在竞选时承诺带来更多的工作岗位、发展和经济繁荣。

sentences.en: But that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但那并没有发生。

sentences.en: There were a lot of embezzlement taking place.
sentences.zh: 发生了大量的贪污盗用。

sentences.en: Instead of lifting up the entire country, the Marcos administration became a notorious kleptocracy.
sentences.zh: 马科斯政府非但没有振兴整个国家，反而成了一个臭名昭著的盗贼统治政权。

sentences.en: So the Marcoses were also known as being incredibly, besides like politically corrupt,
sentences.zh: 所以马科斯家族除了政治腐败之外，

sentences.en: like they were known for like plundering the wealth of the Philippines and saving it for themselves.
sentences.zh: 还以掠夺菲律宾的财富并据为己有而闻名。

sentences.en: Anthony Acampo is a sociology professor who studies the Philippine diaspora.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·奥坎波是一位研究菲律宾人流散的研究社会学教授。

sentences.en: Imelda Marcos, his wife, is famously known for having rooms full of shoes, like hundreds or thousands of pairs of shoes.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子伊梅尔达·马科斯以拥有装满鞋子的房间而闻名，有几百甚至几千双鞋。

sentences.en: As first lady, I have to flaunt love and beauty so that the 50 million Filipinos will see what is perfection.
sentences.zh: 作为第一夫人，我必须炫耀爱与美，以便5000万菲律宾人看到什么是完美。

sentences.en: In their desire to make the Philippines great, they wanted to appear essentially like royalty
sentences.zh: 他们渴望让菲律宾变得伟大，本质上是想表现得像皇室一样

sentences.en: and just looked incredibly expensive and extravagant.
sentences.zh: 看起来极其昂贵和奢华。

sentences.en: You know, Marcos spent a huge amount of the public's funds at that time, which then created inflation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，马科斯当时花费了巨额公共资金，这随后造成了通货膨胀。

sentences.en: It created all of these trade deficits.
sentences.zh: 它造成了所有这些贸易赤字。

sentences.en: Marcos stole billions of dollars from the Philippine economy.
sentences.zh: 马科斯从菲律宾经济中窃取了数十亿美元。

sentences.en: And to offset what he stole, he borrowed more.
sentences.zh: 为了弥补他偷来的钱，他借了更多。

sentences.en: And then it just became cyclical to the point that the Philippines was in huge debt.
sentences.zh: 然后这就变成了一个循环，以至于菲律宾背负了巨额债务。

sentences.en: People did not have jobs, could not subsist on what was being, you know, grown, did not have enough food to eat.
sentences.zh: 人们没有工作，无法靠种植的东西维生，没有足够的食物吃。

sentences.en: And then in 1972, Marcos declared martial law.
sentences.zh: 接着在1972年，马科斯宣布戒严。

sentences.en: I am utilizing this power for the proclamation of martial law to save the republic and reform our social, economic and political institutions in our country.
sentences.zh: 我正在利用这一权力宣布戒严，以拯救共和国，并改革我国的社会、经济和政治体制。

sentences.en: He suspended democracy and basically, like, used his power to, like, fervently suppress any opposition that came.
sentences.zh: 他暂停了民主制度，基本上，可以说是利用自己的权力，狂热地镇压了任何出现的反对声音。

sentences.en: Their vision of the Philippines entailed them disappearing journalists who would speak out against them or activists that would speak out against them and torturing them.
sentences.zh: 他们对菲律宾的设想包括让那些敢于直言反对他们的记者或维权人士人间蒸发，并对他们进行折磨。

sentences.en: By the 1980s, unemployment was high, people were desperate, and Marcos was casting around for a solution.
sentences.zh: 到了二十世纪八十年代，失业率高居不下，人们绝望万分，马科斯开始四处寻找解决方案。

sentences.en: What he landed on was to create an entire economy centered around remittances.
sentences.zh: 他最终想到的办法是建立一个以侨汇为核心的经济体系。

sentences.en: Rather than developing the Philippine economy in and of itself, the Marcos regime would encourage Filipinos to move abroad and maintain ties to the Philippines and send money back.
sentences.zh: 马科斯政权没有选择在国内发展菲律宾经济，而是鼓励菲律宾人出国，同时保持与菲律宾的联系并将钱寄回国。

sentences.en: He basically launched immigration as an economic strategy for the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是将移民作为菲律宾的一项经济战略来推行。

sentences.en: Marcos' plan was twofold.
sentences.zh: 马科斯的计划包含两个方面。

sentences.en: Get Filipinos to leave the country and then make sure they'd send money home, funneling their earnings back into the Philippines' economy.
sentences.zh: 让菲律宾人离开国家，然后确保他们把钱寄回家，将他们的收入汇入菲律宾的经济中。

sentences.en: Marcos' plan came to be known, ironically, as Operation Homecoming.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，马科斯的这项计划后来被称为“荣归行动”。

sentences.en: And it took advantage of a recent change in U.S.
sentences.zh: 它利用了美国近期的一项变革。

sentences.en: immigration law.
sentences.zh: 移民法。

sentences.en: This bill says simply that from this day forth, those wishing to immigrate to America shall be admitted on the basis of their skills.
sentences.zh: 这项法案简单地说，从今天起，希望移民美国的人将根据其技能被准许入境。

sentences.en: The 1965 Immigration Act passed, and that was the legislation that created a pathway for the so-called highly skilled migrants to come.
sentences.zh: 1965年《移民法》通过了，正是这项立法为所谓的“高技能移民”开辟了康庄大道。

sentences.en: Those who can contribute most to this country, to its growth, to its strength, to its spirit, will be the first that are admitted to this land.
sentences.zh: 那些能够对这个国家、对它的发展、对它的力量、对它的精神贡献最多的人，将是最先被允许进入这片土地的人。

sentences.en: While Filipino migrants in the United States in the early 20th century were mainly farm and factory workers in the latter half of the century, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 虽然20世纪初在美国的菲律宾移民主要是农场和工厂工人，但在本世纪的后半叶，美国

sentences.en: opened the gates to a different sector.
sentences.zh: 向另一个领域敞开了大门。

sentences.en: Nursing shortages after World War II had crippled the United States' health care system.
sentences.zh: 二战后的护士短缺曾重创美国的医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: And then, in the 1960s, a second-wave feminism swelled throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 接着，在20世纪60年代，第二波女性主义浪潮在全国范围内高涨。

sentences.en: American women abandoned nursing to pursue other careers.
sentences.zh: 美国女性放弃了护理工作，转而追求其他职业。

sentences.en: Hospital recruiters needed to turn to the thousands of American-trained nurses in the Philippines to fill the shortage.
sentences.zh: 医院招聘人员不得不将目光转向菲律宾数以千计受过美国培训的护士，以填补这一空缺。

sentences.en: And the Philippine government also saw it as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 而菲律宾政府也将此视为一个机遇。

sentences.en: So it was very easy for Marcos to see that as a pathway for employment for Filipinos, but also started to see that as a way to create a remittance economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，马科斯很容易将这视为菲律宾人就业的途径，同时也开始将其视为建立侨汇经济的方法。

sentences.en: But this time, it wasn't just U.S.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，不仅是美国

sentences.en: labor shortages pulling Filipinos abroad.
sentences.zh: 劳动力短缺将菲律宾人吸引到海外。

sentences.en: Marcos went out of his way to incentivize Filipinos to fill labor needs all over the world.
sentences.zh: 马科斯不遗余力地鼓励菲律宾人去填补世界各地的劳动力需求。

sentences.en: Hong Kong, Singapore, Madrid, and all over the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 香港、新加坡、马德里，以及整个中东地区。

sentences.en: The Middle East was experiencing an oil boom during this time.
sentences.zh: 当时中东正经历石油繁荣。

sentences.en: Middle East countries were looking for workers.
sentences.zh: 中东国家正在寻找工人。

sentences.en: To encourage Filipinos to move abroad, Marcos passed the 1974 Labor Code.
sentences.zh: 为了鼓励菲律宾人出国，马科斯通过了1974年《劳动法》。

sentences.en: The law basically secured overseas contract work by establishing recruitment agencies that work with foreign companies to ensure a good wage and basic worker rights.
sentences.zh: 该法律基本上通过建立与外国公司合作的招聘机构，确保丰厚的薪水和基本劳工权益，从而保障了海外合同工的工作。

sentences.en: But only if they went abroad with the sole purpose of sending money back to the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 但前提是他们出国的唯一目的就是把钱寄回菲律宾。

sentences.en: The kind of migration Marcos was encouraging wasn't the kind we think of when people try and start a better life elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 马科斯鼓励的那种移民并不是我们通常所想的那种人们试图在别处开始更好生活的移民。

sentences.en: This national program relied on Filipinos having one foot in the Philippines and one foot out forever.
sentences.zh: 这个国家计划依赖于菲律宾人永远一只脚留在菲律宾，另一只脚踏在外面。

sentences.en: Many of the workers going abroad couldn't bring their families, and the overseas contracts were temporary.
sentences.zh: 许多出国的工人无法携带家属，且海外合同都是临时的。

sentences.en: So there wasn't a pathway to citizenship in those countries after their work was done.
sentences.zh: 因此，工作结束后，他们在那些国家并没有获得公民身份的途径。

sentences.en: But many Filipinos were ready to step up and take part in Operation Homecoming because they needed to.
sentences.zh: 但许多菲律宾人已经准备好挺身而出，参与“荣归行动”，因为他们需要这么做。

sentences.en: I think for Filipinos, the incentive is survival.
sentences.zh: 我认为对菲律宾人来说，动力就是生存。

sentences.en: The conditions that you were living in in the Philippines at that time did not really offer any other opportunity except to leave.
sentences.zh: 那时你在菲律宾的生活条件，除了离开，真的提供不了任何别的机会。

sentences.en: If you want a better life for you and your family, you have to leave.
sentences.zh: 如果你想为你和你的家人过上更好的生活，你必须离开。

sentences.en: Marcos gave these people coming home a new name.
sentences.zh: 马科斯给这些回国的人起了一个新名字。

sentences.en: It actually is a word that emerged when Marcos launched this really aggressive migration plan, economic plan to, like, encourage Filipinos to migrate.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个词，是在马科斯发起这项真正激进的移民计划、经济计划以鼓励菲律宾人移民时诞生的。

sentences.en: Whenever they come back to the Philippines and they visit, what they're called is balikbayans.
sentences.zh: 每当他们回到菲律宾探亲时，人们称他们为“巴里克巴扬”（balikbayans）。

sentences.en: So, like, the homecoming or the return of our people.
sentences.zh: 也就是，我们人民的回家或回归。

sentences.en: He was elevating the status of balikbayans.
sentences.zh: 他在提升“巴里克巴扬”的地位。

sentences.en: As a balikbayan, you're kind of welcomed back to the country as the new aristocrats.
sentences.zh: 作为一名“巴里克巴扬”，你受到这个国家的欢迎，仿佛是新贵族一般。

sentences.en: Balikbayans had a lot of money.
sentences.zh: “巴里克巴扬”有很多钱。

sentences.en: The dollars that they were earning were strong, and they're the new heroes.
sentences.zh: 他们赚的美元很强势，他们是新英雄。

sentences.en: And he said this quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 他经常这么说。

sentences.en: You're the modern-day heroes of the country because your remittances are contributing so much to the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 你们是这个国家的现代英雄，因为你们的侨汇为菲律宾做出了巨大的贡献。

sentences.en: And throughout the 1980s, the balikbayans weren't just sending money home.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪80年代，“巴里克巴扬”不仅往家里寄钱。

sentences.en: They were sending stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们还寄东西。

sentences.en: Even though they were living elsewhere, they kind of maintained ties to the Philippines because they were sending cash.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们住在别处，但他们通过寄现金保持了与菲律宾的某种联系。

sentences.en: But they were also sending goods.
sentences.zh: 但他们也寄送物品。

sentences.en: Sometimes these boxes were gifts letting their loved ones know, I'm thinking about you.
sentences.zh: 有时这些箱子是礼物，让亲人们知道，我一直在想念你们。

sentences.en: But mostly, items inside were essentials that families needed during an economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 但主要来说，里面的物品是家庭在经济危机期间必需的基本物资。

sentences.en: And so, what ended up happening is they would put them in these balikbayan boxes, bring them back.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终发生的情况是，他们会把东西放进这些“巴里克巴扬”箱子里，然后带回来。

sentences.en: And so, the boxes that they would send, you know, everyone loves alliteration.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们寄出的那些箱子，你知道的，大家都喜欢押头韵。

sentences.en: They were called balikbayan boxes.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为“巴里克巴扬”箱。

sentences.en: Unlike Marcos' migration policies designed to bring wealth to the Philippines, this form of remittance, the balikbayan box, happened organically.
sentences.zh: 与旨在为菲律宾带来财富的马科斯移民政策不同，这种汇款形式——“巴里克巴扬”箱，是自发产生的。

sentences.en: When families were separated, they want to remain connected to the families in the Philippines in other ways besides just sending a check home.
sentences.zh: 当家庭分隔两地时，除了寄支票回家，他们还希望通过其他方式与菲律宾的家人保持联系。

sentences.en: The goodies in those boxes often contained mostly American products or things that, you know, Filipinos would imagine, you know, represented the stateside life.
sentences.zh: 这些箱子里的好东西通常大部分包含美国产品，或者你知道的，菲律宾人想象中代表美式生活的事物。

sentences.en: We would open those boxes and think, oh, wow, okay, the chocolates, the Twix, the Folgers coffee, the Colgate, the Gina Tay.
sentences.zh: 我们会打开那些箱子想，哦，哇，好吧，巧克力、特克斯（Twix）巧克力棒、福杰斯（Folgers）咖啡、高露洁、吉娜芒果汁。

sentences.en: I mean, these were like, my God, luxury goods, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些就像是，天哪，奢侈品，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the stateside way of life.
sentences.zh: 这就是美式的生活方式。

sentences.en: And so, it kind of cultivated this sense of, this is what it would mean to live overseas.
sentences.zh: 因此，它在某种程度上培养了一种感觉，即这就是在海外生活意味着什么。

sentences.en: Although Marcos didn't anticipate the balikbayan box, it ended up reinforcing his migration plan.
sentences.zh: 尽管马科斯没有预料到“巴里克巴扬”箱，但它最终巩固了他的移民计划。

sentences.en: First, it was utilitarian in that the balikbayans were supporting their families with both money and boxes of goods.
sentences.zh: 首先，它是务实的，因为“巴里克巴扬”们既用金钱又用一箱箱的物品来支持他们的家人。

sentences.en: But it also helped feed this fantasy of living abroad.
sentences.zh: 但它也有助于滋养这种对海外生活的幻想。

sentences.en: If you become a balikbayan, you too can have access to all these goods.
sentences.zh: 如果你成为一名“巴里克巴扬”，你也可以拥有所有这些物品。

sentences.en: By the mid-1980s, just 10 years after Marcos signed the labor code into law, the number of Filipinos going overseas to work increased by almost 1,000 percent.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪80年代中期，就在马科斯将劳动法签署成为法律的短短10年后，出国工作的菲律宾人数量增加了近1000%。

sentences.en: And as more balikbayans went abroad, more boxes of goods came flowing back.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的“巴里克巴扬”出国，更多一箱箱的物品如潮水般涌回。

sentences.en: To promote the balikbayan box, the Philippine government made it cheaper to ship these boxes, making the items and the cost of shipping duty-free and tax-free.
sentences.zh: 为了推广“巴里克巴扬”箱，菲律宾政府降低了这些箱子的运费，使得物品和运费都免征关税和税收。

sentences.en: But the balikbayan box didn't become the multi-billion-dollar industry it is today until Filipino entrepreneurs in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但直到美国的菲律宾企业家发现了一个商机，“巴里克巴扬”箱才成为如今这个价值数十亿美元的产业。

sentences.en: recognized an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 发现了一个商机。

sentences.en: One of the earliest balikbayan box companies in L.A.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶最早的“巴里克巴扬”箱公司之一

sentences.en: was actually just in a little, like, pop-up in a Philippine grocery store.
sentences.zh: 其实只是菲律宾杂货店里的一个小快闪店。

sentences.en: Anthony Ocampo, the sociology professor at Cal Poly, he actually wrote about the balikbayan box businesses for his Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·奥坎波（Anthony Ocampo），加州州立理工大学的社会学教授，他实际上在自己的博士学位论文中写到了“巴里克巴扬”箱业务。

sentences.en: dissertation.
sentences.zh: 论文。

sentences.en: What's funny is that the sending of boxes by Filipinos is like a multi-billion-dollar industry, but often these companies are just little rented spots in, like, a shopping,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，菲律宾人寄箱子是一个价值数十亿美元的产业，但通常这些公司只是购物中心里租来的小地方，

sentences.en: outdoor shopping plaza.
sentences.zh: 露天购物广场。

sentences.en: Like, if you can imagine, like, that quintessential California, like, outdoor plaza where you'd see, like, a convenience store and a laundromat, there'd also be, like,
sentences.zh: 就像你可以想象的那样，那种典型的加州露天广场，你会看到便利店和自助洗衣店，那里也会有

sentences.en: a balikbayan box company there.
sentences.zh: 一家“巴里克巴扬”箱公司。

sentences.en: Anthony also studied the life cycle of the box, how it travels from one family member to the other all the way across the world.
sentences.zh: 安东尼还研究了箱子的生命周期，它是如何从一个家庭成员跨越大半个地球传给另一个家庭成员的。

sentences.en: Today, more than 10 million Filipinos live overseas, and the more that go overseas, the more boxes get sent back.
sentences.zh: 如今，超过1000万菲律宾人居住在海外，出国的人越多，寄回的箱子就越多。

sentences.en: The box ends up in a boat that travels all the way to the Philippines from the port of Long Beach to the port of Manila.
sentences.zh: 箱子最终被装上一艘船，从长滩港一路航行到马尼拉港，前往菲律宾。

sentences.en: Just imagine, like, a warehouse that's two, three stories high, but, like, the whole room is filled with balikbayan boxes, these huge boxes from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，一个两三层楼高的仓库，整个房间里却塞满了“巴里克巴扬”箱，这些来自世界各地的巨大箱子。

sentences.en: It's bananas.
sentences.zh: 简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: For part of his research, Anthony actually worked for a balikbayan shipping company in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 作为研究的一部分，安东尼实际上在洛杉矶的一家“巴里克巴扬”航运公司工作过。

sentences.en: Waking up at 6 in the morning, 7 in the morning to go pick up balikbayan boxes in a truck with barely any air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 早上6点、7点醒来，坐上一辆几乎没有空调的卡车去收“巴里克巴扬”箱。

sentences.en: Driving to people's homes to pick up balikbayan boxes.
sentences.zh: 开车去人们家里收集“巴里克巴扬”箱。

sentences.en: I remember this, like, 60-something-year-old woman literally got on top of her box and started jumping on it, like, a kid jumping on their bed to get it closed.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个60多岁的女人 literalmente（字面意思上）爬到她的箱子上开始在上面跳蹦，就像小孩在床上跳蹦一样，为了把它合上。

sentences.en: And like any good sociologist, he was most interested in what the box meant to people, how they interacted with it in their lives.
sentences.zh: 就像任何优秀的社会学家一样，他对箱子对人们意味着什么、他们在生活中如何与它互动最感兴趣。

sentences.en: And I remember chatting with her.
sentences.zh: 我记得和她聊天。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, who's the box for?
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，这箱子是给谁的？

sentences.en: And she's like, oh, it's for my son in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，这是给我在菲律宾的儿子的。

sentences.en: You know, he's doing so well over there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他在那边过得很好。

sentences.en: He's getting married.
sentences.zh: 他要结婚了。

sentences.en: And then I asked her, or are you going to be going to the wedding?
sentences.zh: 然后我问她，那你打算去参加婚礼吗？

sentences.en: And I just saw the mood on her face get really sad.
sentences.zh: 我看到她脸上的情绪变得非常悲伤。

sentences.en: And she's like, no, I'm not going to be able to go.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，我没办法去。

sentences.en: And I just thought, oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哦，哇。

sentences.en: This is, like, one of those moments where you see, like, the box is kind of supposed to fill the void of your absence.
sentences.zh: 这就像是这样的时刻，你看到箱子本意似乎是为了填补你缺席的空虚。

sentences.en: But it never fully fills the void.
sentences.zh: 但它从未完全填满这种空虚。

sentences.en: And I remember taking the box away and the older Filipino woman was, like, just watching us from the balcony.
sentences.zh: 我记得把箱子搬走时，那个菲律宾老妇人就在阳台上看着我们。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was like, take care of the box.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像是在说，照顾好箱子。

sentences.en: Make sure it doesn't break.
sentences.zh: 确保它不会破损。

sentences.en: Anthony found a similar longing when he followed those Balak Bayan boxes to their recipients in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 安东尼在追随那些“巴里克巴扬”箱到菲律宾的收件人时，也发现了类似的渴望。

sentences.en: He remembers one box in particular sent by a father in San Diego to his adult son in Manila.
sentences.zh: 他记得其中有一个特别的箱子，是由圣迭戈的一位父亲寄给他远在马尼拉的成年儿子的。

sentences.en: He said, you know, what's interesting is my dad, whenever he sends a box, he sends me pictures of cranes, like construction cranes.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，有趣的是，我爸爸每次寄箱子，都会给我寄一些起重机的照片，比如建筑起重机。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's what I was really into when I was eight years old.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那正是我八岁时非常着迷的东西。

sentences.en: And my dad, even like 12, 15 years later, he still thinks I'm into cranes.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸，甚至在12、15年后，还是觉得我对起重机感兴趣。

sentences.en: And I don't have the heart to tell him that that's not who I am anymore.
sentences.zh: 我又不忍心告诉他我已经不是那样的人了。

sentences.en: What does it look like for a country to be built on remittances?
sentences.zh: 一个建立在侨汇之上的国家会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Like, how does that shape an identity of a country?
sentences.zh: 比如，这如何塑造一个国家的身份认同？

sentences.en: I think if a country's economic development plan is based on immigration,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果一个国家的经济发展计划基于移民，

sentences.en: what that means is that there's a whole lot of its citizens that are going to be just like cognitively oriented toward building a life outside of the country they were born in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着会有相当多的公民，他们的认知导向就是要在他们出生国之外的地方建立生活。

sentences.en: And Filipinos, we have such tight-knit families, we have strong families, but it's a country where people are encouraged to separate from their families for decades.
sentences.zh: 而菲律宾人，我们的家庭联系如此紧密，我们有着强大的家庭观念，但这却是一个鼓励人们与家人分离数十年的国家。

sentences.en: And, you know, no matter how beautiful this Balak Bayan box is or whatever nice things are in it,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，无论这个“巴里克巴扬”箱有多精美，或者里面有什么好东西，

sentences.en: it doesn't fill the gap that happens when a loved one is just not under the same roof as you anymore.
sentences.zh: 它都无法弥补当至亲不再与你同在一个屋檐下时所产生的空缺。

sentences.en: My Lola, who received Balak Bayan boxes from my uncle Dennis when she lived in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 我的外祖母（Lola），她住在菲律宾时收到了我舅舅丹尼斯寄来的“巴里克巴扬”箱。

sentences.en: The Balak Bayan box, it came from Kuya Dennis.
sentences.zh: “巴里克巴扬”箱，它来自丹尼斯表哥（Kuya Dennis）。

sentences.en: It came from his heart.
sentences.zh: 它发自他的真心。

sentences.en: She moved to the United States decades later.
sentences.zh: 几十年后她搬到了美国。

sentences.en: But while coming here allowed her to connect with some of her kids in the United States, she had to leave her youngest son, Ariel, who was still in school.
sentences.zh: 但来到这里虽然让她得以与在美国的一些孩子团聚，她却不得不留下还在上学的小儿子阿里尔（Ariel）。

sentences.en: And then she became the one sending Balak Bayan boxes.
sentences.zh: 然后她成了那个寄“巴里克巴扬”箱的人。

sentences.en: Whenever I ate something, like the chocolate, oh, I remember Ariel loves this chocolate.
sentences.zh: 每当我吃某种东西，比如巧克力，哦，我就会想阿里尔最爱这种巧克力了。

sentences.en: So I'll go to Costco and it's like when you're homesick and you miss your son, I buy something for them and then put it in a box.
sentences.zh: 所以我就会去Costco，这就像当你思乡想念儿子时，我为他们买点东西然后放进箱子里。

sentences.en: That makes me happy that my homesick will be cured because of that.
sentences.zh: 这让我很高兴，因为这能治愈我的乡愁。

sentences.en: Thinking about my own family's history, I don't really know how to hold that happiness with the reality of why we send the Balak Bayan box in the first place.
sentences.zh: 想到自己家族的历史，我真的不知道该如何将这种快乐与我们最初为什么要寄“巴里克巴扬”箱的现实结合起来。

sentences.en: On the one hand, I feel sad when I think about my Lola always being oceans away from her children for these big historical and economic reasons far beyond our control.
sentences.zh: 一方面，每当想到由于这些超出我们控制的宏大历史和经济原因，我的外祖母总是与她的孩子们远隔重洋，我就感到难过。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, there's something beautiful about her, knowing that her son in the Philippines would like it,
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，她知道她在菲律宾的儿子会喜欢它，

sentences.en: and then going out of her way to buy boxes and boxes of that chocolate to send to him.
sentences.zh: 然后不辞辛劳地买了一箱又一箱那种巧克力寄给他，这其中有一种美妙的东西。

sentences.en: Why do you say your homesick will be cured?
sentences.zh: 你为什么说你的乡愁会被治愈？

sentences.en: Because whenever I think of them and I give them something that I have here and not in the Philippines, that makes me happy.
sentences.zh: 因为每当我思念他们时，我把我有而菲律宾没有的东西送给他们，这让我感到高兴。

sentences.en: When we come back after the break, Gabby tells us about the salty, delicious, artery-clogging item that you can find in almost every Balak Bayan box after this.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，加比将为我们讲述那个咸香美味、让人胆固醇飙升，你几乎能在每一个“巴里克巴扬”箱里找到的物品，广告之后见。

sentences.en: So, Gabby, you're back to tell us about the in-depth, surprisingly deep story of one specific item found in the typical Balak Bayan box.
sentences.zh: 那么，加比，你回来了，要跟我们讲讲那个典型的“巴里克巴扬”箱里发现的某种特定物品的深入且出人意料的故事。

sentences.en: And it's actually an item you made an entire three-part series about last year for WNYC and The Atlantic, their podcast called The Experiment.
sentences.zh: 这其实是你去年为WNYC和《大西洋月刊》的播客节目《实验》（The Experiment）制作了一个完整的三部分系列的物品。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what that item is?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我那是什么物品吗？

sentences.en: So this item that I made an entire three-part series about is the salty, delicious, and surprisingly profound Spam.
sentences.zh: 我制作了一个完整三部分系列的这个物品，就是咸香美味且出人意料深奥的午餐肉（Spam）。

sentences.en: So why did you decide to make an entire series about Spam?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么决定为午餐肉制作一个完整的系列节目呢？

sentences.en: Okay, so the main reason was that my Filipino family and Pacific Islanders in general love Spam.
sentences.zh: 好的，主要原因是我的菲律宾家人以及整个太平洋岛民都非常喜欢午餐肉。

sentences.en: I find this really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我发现这真的非常迷人。

sentences.en: So I grew up never thinking of Spam as anything other than not very good meat, like super processed.
sentences.zh: 我从小到大从未把午餐肉看作是别的什么东西，只觉得它是不太好的肉，属于超级加工食品。

sentences.en: You know, it kind of fits into the hyper-processed American food that is not appealing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它有点符合那种没有吸引力的高度加工美国食品。

sentences.en: And I don't know if I even had it for most of my life.
sentences.zh: 我不知道在我大半生中是否甚至吃过它。

sentences.en: And then I met Joy, my partner, and she's Filipino.
sentences.zh: 然后我遇到了乔伊（Joy），我的伴侣，她是菲律宾人。

sentences.en: And now I have Spam way more than I ever thought I would.
sentences.zh: 现在我吃午餐肉的频率比我以往任何时候想象的都要多。

sentences.en: And I like it a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢它。

sentences.en: And her family loves Spam.
sentences.zh: 她的家人也非常喜欢午餐肉。

sentences.en: And it's just one of the things that's part of my life now.
sentences.zh: 而且这已经成了我生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的。

sentences.en: So that feels like a very common story to just like set, you know, once you're part of a Filipino community, Spam is just like going to be part of your life from now on.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来是个很普遍的故事，你知道的，一旦你加入了菲律宾社群，午餐肉就会成为你以后生活的一部分。

sentences.en: It'll be a family member.
sentences.zh: 它就像个家庭成员。

sentences.en: And I wanted to try and understand why that is for Filipinos.
sentences.zh: 我想试着去理解为什么菲律宾人会这样。

sentences.en: And like what I found was that has a lot to do with the American quest to spread democracy abroad.
sentences.zh: 我发现这其实很大程度上与美国在海外传播民主的诉求有关。

sentences.en: So what I mean is during World War II, Spam was one of the key food sources in what was called the K-rations for American GIs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在二战期间，午餐肉是美国大兵所谓的“K口粮”中的关键食物来源之一。

sentences.en: Spam has a lot of calories.
sentences.zh: 午餐肉热量很高。

sentences.en: It stores well.
sentences.zh: 它很容易保存。

sentences.en: So it's perfect for soldiers.
sentences.zh: 所以它对士兵来说是完美的食物。

sentences.en: And when the Philippines became a central battleground for the United States to fight the Japanese, American soldiers landed in Manila.
sentences.zh: 当菲律宾成为美国打击日本的主战场时，美军士兵在马尼拉登陆。

sentences.en: And with them, so did the Spam and their food rations.
sentences.zh: 随着他们一同到达的，还有午餐肉和他们的军粮。

sentences.en: And just to put this into context, in total, 150 million pounds of Spam were produced for the war effort during World War II.
sentences.zh: 为了说明这一点，在二战期间，为了战争需要总共生产了1.5亿磅的午餐肉。

sentences.en: So you can only imagine how much of that is ending up in the Philippines during that time.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，当时有多少午餐肉最终流向了菲律宾。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the irony of American soldiers eating Spam morning, noon, and night is that they got so completely sick of it.
sentences.zh: 美国士兵早也吃晚也吃午餐肉，讽刺的是，他们吃得彻底腻烦了。

sentences.en: They would trade their Spam with locals for literally anything else that wasn't this nondescript slab of pink salty meat.
sentences.zh: 他们会用午餐肉跟当地人交换任何其他东西，只要不是这块毫无特色、又粉又咸的肉就行。

sentences.en: A delicious nondescript slab of pink salty meat.
sentences.zh: 一块美味却毫无特色、又粉又咸的肉。

sentences.en: But I can imagine not wanting to eat it every day.
sentences.zh: 不过我可以理解为什么不想天天吃它。

sentences.en: And so they traded it far and wide.
sentences.zh: 所以他们到处交换。

sentences.en: And a lot of it ended up in the hands of local Filipinos who began to love it.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分落入了当地菲律宾人的手中，他们开始喜欢上了它。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's definitely part of the story.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: But also, Spam really holds this very sentimental value for Filipinos who went through Japanese occupation.
sentences.zh: 但同时，对于经历过日本占领的菲律宾人来说，午餐肉确实有着非常深厚的情感价值。

sentences.en: My grandpa, my Lolo, was around eight or nine years old when American GIs started to come to the Philippines in droves.
sentences.zh: 我的爷爷，也就是我的Lolo，当美军大兵成群结队来到菲律宾时，他大约八九岁。

sentences.en: And he remembers hiding in the mountains from the Japanese army and, like, spending months feeling hungry and scared with his family.
sentences.zh: 他记得自己和家人为了躲避日军而藏在山里，饥饿和恐惧的日子持续了好几个月。

sentences.en: So when American GIs came and, like, started rolling through the dusty mountain roads in their trucks, this was a big deal for them.
sentences.zh: 所以当美军乘卡车滚滚驶过尘土飞扬的山路时，这对他们来说是一件大事。

sentences.en: And the American GIs would throw stuff to Filipinos lining the road.
sentences.zh: 美军会向路边排队的菲律宾人扔东西。

sentences.en: So cookies, cigarettes, chocolate.
sentences.zh: 比如饼干、香烟、巧克力。

sentences.en: Probably had some downsides with cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 烟草可能带来了一些负面影响。

sentences.en: And, of course, cans of Spam.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一罐罐的午餐肉。

sentences.en: So my grandfather tells the story of, you know, chasing after the trucks and catching cans of Spam as the trucks were kind of rolling by.
sentences.zh: 我爷爷讲过这样一个故事：卡车缓缓开过时，他追着卡车去接住扔过来的午餐肉罐头。

sentences.en: And he's not alive anymore, so I can't ask him this.
sentences.zh: 他已经不在了，所以我没法再问他。

sentences.en: But I always wondered if, you know, that was the first time he had ever seen an American.
sentences.zh: 但我总是在想，那是不是他第一次见到美国人？

sentences.en: Like, of his introduction to, like, America were American GIs tossing cans of Spam at him during World War II.
sentences.zh: 就好像他对美国的初印象，就是在二战期间美军士兵朝他扔午餐肉罐头。

sentences.en: That's a strong sentimental linkage to, like, this army that is helping free people and then giving them food to people who are hungry.
sentences.zh: 这与这支军队有着强烈的情感联系，他们帮助解放人民，然后把食物给饥饿的人。

sentences.en: That's really intense.
sentences.zh: 这真的很强烈。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So to him, it was like, Spam represented freedom.
sentences.zh: 所以对他来说，午餐肉代表着自由。

sentences.en: And this was a very common experience in the Philippines for people in my Lolo's generation.
sentences.zh: 对于我爷爷那一辈人来说，这在菲律宾是一种非常普遍的经历。

sentences.en: Spam symbolized, like, luxury, abundance, and American freedom.
sentences.zh: 午餐肉象征着奢侈、丰盛和美国的自由。

sentences.en: And after that, Spam became this prized delicacy in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，午餐肉成了菲律宾备受珍视的美味。

sentences.en: And that's why it's still a quintessential item today in Balak Bayon boxes.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它今天仍然是“巴拉巴勇”（Balikbayan）礼盒中的标志性物品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I understand that for someone like your Lolo's generation, that Spam represents, you know, all good things about American culture.
sentences.zh: 所以我理解，对于像你爷爷那一辈人来说，午餐肉代表着美国文化中所有美好的东西。

sentences.en: But I'm curious if that love of Spam extends to someone like you.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，这种对午餐肉的热爱是否延伸到了像你这样的人身上？

sentences.en: Like, how do you feel about Spam?
sentences.zh: 比如，你对午餐肉有什么感觉？

sentences.en: So obviously I have a really sentimental attachment to it because of my grandpa and how much he loved it.
sentences.zh: 所以显然我对它有着很深的情感依恋，因为我的爷爷以及他有多么喜欢它。

sentences.en: And also when I would come home as a kid with, like, good grades or something from, you know, from school, my mom would make me a special Spam breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且当我小时候考了高分或者从学校回来时，我妈妈会给我做一个特别的午餐肉早餐。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Rice, eggs.
sentences.zh: 米饭，鸡蛋。

sentences.en: Rice, fried egg.
sentences.zh: 米饭，煎蛋。

sentences.en: Fried Spam.
sentences.zh: 煎午餐肉。

sentences.en: Fried Spam.
sentences.zh: 煎午餐肉。

sentences.en: Fried garlic.
sentences.zh: 炸大蒜。

sentences.en: Oh, lovely.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我超爱它。

sentences.en: But I also have this love-hate relationship with it.
sentences.zh: 但我对它也是又爱又恨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Love because it's always been this distinctly Filipino thing to me.
sentences.zh: 爱是因为对我来说这始终是一种鲜明的菲律宾特色。

sentences.en: And when my Lolo was alive, he loved Spam.
sentences.zh: 我Lolo活着的时候，他很爱午餐肉。

sentences.en: And when he came to America, where Spam was freely available and it wasn't a luxury item, he would still eat it all the time, like, every day for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 当他来到美国、这里的午餐肉随处可见且不再是奢侈品时，他仍然经常吃，比如每天早餐都吃。

sentences.en: That was until he got diagnosed with diabetes.
sentences.zh: 直到他被诊断出患有糖尿病。

sentences.en: And when he was diagnosed, his doctor was like, the Spam needs to be the first thing to go.
sentences.zh: 确诊后，他的医生说，午餐肉必须是第一个戒掉的东西。

sentences.en: And so there's this negative connotation for it with me.
sentences.zh: 所以它对我来说有一种负面的联想。

sentences.en: You know, American imperialism and American canned goods imported to the Philippines have done a lot of harm in terms of public health.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，美国帝国主义和进口到菲律宾的美国罐头食品在公众健康方面造成了很大损害。

sentences.en: Like, my Lolo, for example, died of complications from diabetes a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 比如我Lolo，几年前就死于糖尿病并发症。

sentences.en: Diabetes is in, like, all of my family members have diabetes.
sentences.zh: 糖尿病在……可以说我所有的家庭成员都有糖尿病。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that it's because of Spam.
sentences.zh: 我不是说这是因为午餐肉。

sentences.en: But the widespread export of, like, unhealthy processed American foods and, like, the reverence for it, processed foods like Spam, for me, is part of, like,
sentences.zh: 但对不健康的美国加工食品的大规模出口以及对它的推崇，像午餐肉这样的加工食品，在我看来是……

sentences.en: the real public health issue in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 菲律宾真正的公共健康问题的一部分。

sentences.en: And diabetes and heart disease are some of the leading causes of death in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 糖尿病和心脏病是菲律宾人的主要死因之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is pretty widespread.
sentences.zh: 而且这相当普遍。

sentences.en: Like, everything that we export that's processed and high in fat and high in salt and high in sugar, you know, this is something not unique to the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 我们出口的所有加工食品，都是高脂肪、高盐、高糖的，你知道的，这并非菲律宾独有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's widespread, especially throughout the Pacific Islands.
sentences.zh: 而且它很普遍，尤其是在整个太平洋岛屿。

sentences.en: Wherever American GIs went during World War II, they left a trail of fatty, salty American processed foods in their wake.
sentences.zh: 二战期间美军去过的地方，身后都留下一串高脂肪、高盐的美国加工食品。

sentences.en: And Spam has become really integrated into local cuisines in places like Hawaii, Guam, American Samoa.
sentences.zh: 午餐肉已经真正融入了夏威夷、关岛、美属萨摩亚等地的当地饮食中。

sentences.en: And all of those places have, like, staggeringly high rates of diabetes and heart disease.
sentences.zh: 所有这些地方的糖尿病和心脏病发病率都高得惊人。

sentences.en: So, the story I thought I was telling through the Spam series was, you know, that Spam was delicious and a relic of imperialism.
sentences.zh: 所以，我原本以为通过午餐肉系列讲述的故事是，午餐肉很美味，而且是帝国主义的遗物。

sentences.en: The end.
sentences.zh: 故事讲完了。

sentences.en: But when I started researching Spam, and especially when I went to visit Spam's headquarters in Austin, Minnesota, that's when I really opened Pandora's can, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 但当我开始研究午餐肉，尤其是当我参观位于明尼苏达州奥斯汀的午餐肉总部时，可以说是打开了潘多拉的罐子。

sentences.en: I found out that the factory that makes Spam actually played a huge role in the American labor movement in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 我发现制造午餐肉的工厂实际上在20世纪80年代的美国劳工运动中发挥了巨大作用。

sentences.en: And that story led us into a larger story about immigration, the history of meatpacking, the evolution of labor.
sentences.zh: 这个故事把我们引向了关于移民、肉类加工史和劳工演变的更大故事。

sentences.en: And it ended up being that the story of Spam crisscrosses, like, decades and continents.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，午餐肉的故事跨越了数十年和各大洲。

sentences.en: And it touches some modern pressing questions about food, family, and how we want to work to put food on the table.
sentences.zh: 它触及了关于食物、家庭以及我们如何通过工作来谋生的现代紧迫问题。

sentences.en: Well, it is all really fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实都非常迷人。

sentences.en: So, if people want to hear more, and I really recommend they do, they should check out WNYC's and the Atlantic's The Experiment podcast from last spring.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人们想了解更多——我强烈建议他们去听听，他们应该去收听WNYC和大西洋月刊（The Atlantic）去年春天推出的播客节目《实验》（The Experiment）。

sentences.en: There's a three-part series on Spam, how the American dream got canned.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个关于午餐肉的三集系列节目，讲述了美国梦是如何被装进罐头的。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Gabby.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，加比（Gabby）。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
